title: Past Events, Time & Conversations
subtitle: Use past simple, talk about time, and keep a conversation going.

sections.label: Lesson Notes
sections.title: What we explored
sections.intro: We practised useful vocabulary, listened to stories about unexpected meetings, reviewed past simple and in / on / at for time, and practised a conversation with a fellow traveller.

cards.title: Past events
cards.text: Use past simple for actions that finished before now. After did or didn’t, use the base verb.

cards.title: Time phrases
cards.text: Use in for months, years and parts of the day; on for days and dates; at for clock times and night.

cards.title: Keep a conversation going
cards.text: Ask a relevant follow-up question about travel, work, hobbies or the weather.

patterns.label: A finished action
patterns.explanation: Use the past form for an action that is complete.

patterns.label: A negative
patterns.explanation: After didn’t, use the base verb.

patterns.label: Time
patterns.explanation: On + day; at + clock time; in + month or year.

questions.q: I ___ a film last night.
questions.explanation: Watched is the past form for a completed action last night.

questions.q: She didn’t ___ to work yesterday.
questions.explanation: After didn’t, use the base verb go.

questions.q: ___ you see your friend on Saturday?
questions.explanation: Did starts a question about a finished past action.

questions.q: We met ___ Monday.
The train arrived ___ 8:15.
questions.explanation: Use at with a clock time.

questions.q: They travelled ___ July.
He ___ his keys yesterday.
questions.explanation: Lost is the past form of lose.

questions.q: I called my sister two days ___.
Choose the correct message.
questions.explanation: After Did, use the base verb call.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation: After didn’t, use go, not went.

questions.q: The meeting was ___ Friday morning.
We usually sleep ___ night.
questions.explanation: At night is a common fixed time phrase.

questions.q: My family moved here ___ 2022.
What ___ you do yesterday?
questions.explanation: Use Did in a past simple question.

questions.q: We ___ lunch at one o’clock.
questions.explanation: Had is the past form of have.

cards.title: confidence
cards.meaning: a feeling that you can do something well

cards.title: compartment
cards.meaning: a separate small space in a train or bag
cards.example: Our bags were in the train compartment.

cards.title: get something off your chest
cards.meaning: talk about a problem that has been worrying you
cards.example: He needed to get it off his chest.

cards.title: stranger
cards.meaning: a person you do not know
cards.example: She started a conversation with a stranger.

cards.title: fellow traveller
cards.example: A fellow traveller asked about my trip.

readings.title: A conversation on the train
readings.text: Last Friday, Eren travelled by train to visit his cousin. He sat near the window and put his bag in the compartment above his seat. A fellow traveller smiled and asked, “Is this your first time in Ankara?” Eren said no, but explained that he had not visited for two years. They talked about work, food and the rainy weather. The conversation made the journey feel much shorter.

questions.q: Where did Eren travel?
Where did he put his bag?
opt: In the compartment above his seat

questions.q: What did they talk about?
Eren travelled on Friday.
It was Eren’s first visit to Ankara.
The conversation made the journey feel shorter.

readings.title: A difficult week
readings.text: Mina had a busy week at work. On Tuesday, she stayed late to finish a report. On Wednesday evening, she met a friend for coffee and talked about her worries. She needed to get something off her chest. Her friend listened carefully and asked useful questions. By the end of the conversation, Mina felt calmer and more confident about the next day.

questions.q: Why did Mina stay late on Tuesday?
When did she meet her friend?
How did Mina feel after the conversation?
Mina had a busy week.
Her friend ignored her worries.
Her friend asked useful questions.

readings.title: Buying a new phone
readings.text: Two months ago, Can needed a new phone. He looked at several models online, but he did not buy one immediately. On Saturday, he went to a shop because he wanted to hold the phones and try the cameras. A salesperson explained the differences clearly. Can bought a phone that afternoon because it was easy to use and the price was reasonable.

questions.q: What did Can need?
Why did he go to a shop?
opt: To hold the phones and try the cameras

questions.q: When did he buy the phone?
Can looked at models online.
He bought a phone immediately online.
A salesperson explained the differences.

sections.label: Role-play
sections.title: Conversation practice
sections.intro: Choose a natural reply in each chat turn. Then switch roles and choose the best question to keep the conversation moving.

questions.q: Fellow traveller: “Is this your first time in Ankara?” Choose your reply.
opt: No, but I haven’t visited for two years.

questions.q: Fellow traveller: “What brings you here?” Choose your reply.
opt: I’m visiting my cousin for the weekend.

questions.q: Fellow traveller: “Do you like travelling by train?” Choose your reply.
opt: Yes, it’s relaxing and I can read.

questions.q: Now you ask a question. Choose the best follow-up.
Traveller: “I’m going to see my family.” Choose a natural reply.
opt: That sounds lovely. How long are you staying?

questions.q: Traveller: “I work in IT.” Choose a relevant question.
opt: What kind of work do you do?

questions.q: Traveller: “I like playing online games.” Choose a suitable reply.
opt: What games do you enjoy playing?

questions.q: Choose a friendly way to end the conversation.
opt: It was nice talking to you. Enjoy your trip!
